finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker could inject malicious characters into the email content, which could be interpreted as a command by the shell.
finding.assumptions: The email content is attacker-controlled and contains malicious characters.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: If the email content size exceeds the allocated buffer size, it could lead to a buffer overflow.
finding.assumptions: The email content size is not properly validated before being copied to the buffer.

finding.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
finding.trigger: If the email content contains malicious scripts, it could be executed in the context of the application.
finding.assumptions: The email content is rendered in a web application without proper sanitization.

finding.title: Insecure Direct Object References
finding.trigger: If the email content is used to reference files or resources directly, an attacker could exploit this to access unauthorized files.
finding.assumptions: The email content is used to reference files or resources without proper access control.
